# homarr_invite (Resource)

Manages a Homarr registration invite.

Requires an admin API key and the `credentials` auth provider. The invite link a person follows is `https://<your-homarr>/auth/invite/<id>?token=<token>`.

**Lifecycle.** An invite works once. Registering through it deletes it, so the next refresh drops it from state and the apply after that creates a new invite, with a new token and link. Remove the resource once its invite has been used, or rotate it on purpose — for instance by taking `expiration_date` from a `time_rotating` resource, since changing it replaces the invite.

An invite stops working at `expiration_date`, but Homarr never deletes expired invites: they stay in Homarr, and in state, until destroyed. Homarr also accepts an expiration date in the past, which creates an invite that can never be used.

Homarr deletes an invite together with the user that created it — the user behind the API key. Deleting that user, for example in the UI, removes every invite it created, and the next apply recreates them with new tokens and links. `homarr_user` refuses to destroy or replace the user behind the provider's own key on Homarr 2.3.0 and newer, so through Terraform this happens only when the invites were created with another key.

The `token` exists in state only when Terraform created the invite: Homarr returns it once, in the creation response, so an imported invite has none.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "homarr_invite" "onboarding" {
  expiration_date = "2027-06-01T00:00:00Z"
}

# The token is returned by Homarr exactly once, at creation, and is stored in
# state. Assemble the link users follow from the id and the token.
output "invite_url" {
  value     = "https://homarr.example.com/auth/invite/${homarr_invite.onboarding.id}?token=${homarr_invite.onboarding.token}"
  sensitive = true
}

# An invite works once: registering through it deletes it, and the next apply
# creates a new one. To hand out a fresh link on a schedule instead, derive the
# expiration from a rotating timestamp: changing it replaces the invite.
resource "time_rotating" "weekly" {
  rotation_days = 7
}

resource "homarr_invite" "weekly" {
  expiration_date = time_rotating.weekly.rotation_rfc3339
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `expiration_date` (String) Moment the invite stops working, as an RFC 3339 timestamp such as `2027-01-01T00:00:00Z` or `2027-01-01T02:00:00+02:00`. It must be a whole second, because Homarr stores the date in whole seconds on SQLite: a value such as `2027-01-01T00:00:00.5Z` is rejected, while a zero fraction such as `.000` is allowed. `T` and `Z` must be upper case, and an offset must be written `+hh:mm` or `-hh:mm`.

~> **Note** Homarr has no endpoint to extend an invite, so changing this forces a new invite — and therefore a new token and link.

### Read-Only

- `creator_id` (String) Identifier of the user that created the invite — the user behind the API key.
- `creator_name` (String) Name of the user that created the invite.
- `id` (String) Homarr-generated identifier of the invite.
- `token` (String, Sensitive) Secret token that completes the invite link. Homarr returns it exactly once, at creation, and never again — it is stored in Terraform state and cannot be recovered if lost.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `identity` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = homarr_invite.onboarding
  identity = {
    id = "pvt1o8h5a86rsmm8h76pprkg"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
### Identity Schema

#### Required

- `id` (String) Homarr-generated identifier of the invite.

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
# The token is not recoverable, so it is null after an import.
import {
  to = homarr_invite.onboarding
  id = "pvt1o8h5a86rsmm8h76pprkg"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Invites are imported by id. The token is not recoverable — Homarr omits it from
# every response after creation — so it will be null in state.
terraform import homarr_invite.onboarding pvt1o8h5a86rsmm8h76pprkg
```
